Fundamentals of Molecular Biology & Gene.question: 1) The basic structural unit of DNA is the:
Fundamentals of Molecular Biology & Gene.exp: DNA is composed of nucleotides, each consisting of a nitrogenous base, deoxyribose sugar and phosphate group.

Fundamentals of Molecular Biology & Gene.question: 2) Which nitrogenous base is found only in DNA?
Fundamentals of Molecular Biology & Gene.exp: Thymine is unique to DNA, whereas uracil replaces thymine in RNA.

Fundamentals of Molecular Biology & Gene.question: 3) Which nitrogenous base is present in RNA instead of thymine?
Fundamentals of Molecular Biology & Gene.exp: RNA contains uracil, which pairs with adenine during transcription and translation.

Fundamentals of Molecular Biology & Gene.question: 4) DNA replication occurs during which phase of the cell cycle?
Fundamentals of Molecular Biology & Gene.exp: DNA synthesis and chromosome duplication occur during the synthesis (S) phase.

Fundamentals of Molecular Biology & Gene.question: 5) DNA replication is described as:
Fundamentals of Molecular Biology & Gene.exp: Each daughter DNA molecule contains one parental strand and one newly synthesized strand.

Fundamentals of Molecular Biology & Gene.question: 6) The enzyme responsible for synthesizing new DNA strands is:
Fundamentals of Molecular Biology & Gene.exp: DNA polymerase catalyzes the addition of nucleotides during DNA replication.

Fundamentals of Molecular Biology & Gene.question: 7) The enzyme that unwinds the DNA double helix during replication is:
Fundamentals of Molecular Biology & Gene.exp: Helicase separates the two DNA strands by breaking hydrogen bonds.

Fundamentals of Molecular Biology & Gene.question: 8) DNA ligase is responsible for:
Fundamentals of Molecular Biology & Gene.exp: DNA ligase seals phosphodiester bonds between adjacent DNA fragments on the lagging strand.

Fundamentals of Molecular Biology & Gene.question: 9) The process of synthesis of RNA from a DNA template is called:
Fundamentals of Molecular Biology & Gene.exp: During transcription, RNA polymerase synthesizes RNA using DNA as the template.

Fundamentals of Molecular Biology & Gene.question: 10) Messenger RNA carries genetic information from:
Fundamentals of Molecular Biology & Gene.exp: mRNA transports the genetic code from the nucleus to ribosomes for protein synthesis.

Fundamentals of Molecular Biology & Gene.question: 11) The process of protein synthesis from mRNA is known as:
Fundamentals of Molecular Biology & Gene.exp: During translation, ribosomes decode the mRNA sequence to synthesize proteins.

Fundamentals of Molecular Biology & Gene.question: 12) The site of protein synthesis in the cell is the:
Fundamentals of Molecular Biology & Gene.exp: Ribosomes translate mRNA into polypeptide chains using transfer RNA.

Fundamentals of Molecular Biology & Gene.question: 13) Transfer RNA (tRNA) functions by:
Fundamentals of Molecular Biology & Gene.option1: Carrying genetic information to the nucleus
Fundamentals of Molecular Biology & Gene.option3: Carrying amino acids to the ribosome
Fundamentals of Molecular Biology & Gene.exp: Each tRNA transports a specific amino acid and recognizes the corresponding codon on mRNA.

Fundamentals of Molecular Biology & Gene.question: 14) The three-base sequence on mRNA that codes for an amino acid is called a:
Fundamentals of Molecular Biology & Gene.exp: Each codon consists of three nucleotides specifying one amino acid or a stop signal.

Fundamentals of Molecular Biology & Gene.question: 15) The complementary three-base sequence on tRNA is known as the:
Fundamentals of Molecular Biology & Gene.exp: The anticodon pairs with the complementary codon on mRNA during translation.

Fundamentals of Molecular Biology & Gene.question: 16) Which codon usually initiates protein synthesis?
Fundamentals of Molecular Biology & Gene.exp: AUG is the initiation codon and codes for methionine in eukaryotes.

Fundamentals of Molecular Biology & Gene.question: 17) Which of the following is a stop codon?
Fundamentals of Molecular Biology & Gene.exp: UAA, UAG and UGA are termination codons that signal the end of translation.

Fundamentals of Molecular Biology & Gene.question: 18) A mutation that changes one amino acid to another is called a:
Fundamentals of Molecular Biology & Gene.exp: A missense mutation results in substitution of one amino acid for another in the protein.

Fundamentals of Molecular Biology & Gene.question: 19) A mutation that introduces a premature stop codon is called a:
Fundamentals of Molecular Biology & Gene.exp: Nonsense mutations terminate protein synthesis prematurely, producing truncated proteins.

Fundamentals of Molecular Biology & Gene.question: 20) Insertion or deletion of nucleotides not in multiples of three produces a:
Fundamentals of Molecular Biology & Gene.exp: Frameshift mutations alter the reading frame, usually causing marked changes in the resulting protein.

Fundamentals of Molecular Biology & Gene.question: 21) The normal human somatic cell contains:
Fundamentals of Molecular Biology & Gene.exp: Human somatic cells contain 46 chromosomes arranged in 23 pairs.

Fundamentals of Molecular Biology & Gene.question: 22) Human gametes normally contain:
Fundamentals of Molecular Biology & Gene.exp: Gametes are haploid and contain one chromosome from each homologous pair.

Fundamentals of Molecular Biology & Gene.question: 23) Down syndrome is most commonly caused by:
Fundamentals of Molecular Biology & Gene.exp: Down syndrome results most commonly from meiotic nondisjunction leading to an extra chromosome 21.

Fundamentals of Molecular Biology & Gene.question: 24) Turner syndrome is characterized by:
Fundamentals of Molecular Biology & Gene.exp: Turner syndrome results from complete or partial absence of one X chromosome.

Fundamentals of Molecular Biology & Gene.question: 25) A child presents with intellectual disability, upward-slanting palpebral fissures, hypotonia and a single transverse palmar crease. The most likely chromosomal abnormality is:
Fundamentals of Molecular Biology & Gene.exp: These classic clinical features are characteristic of Down syndrome caused by trisomy 21.

Fundamentals of Molecular Biology & Gene.question: 26) Klinefelter syndrome is characterized by the karyotype:
Fundamentals of Molecular Biology & Gene.exp: Klinefelter syndrome results from an extra X chromosome in males and commonly presents with infertility, small testes and gynecomastia.

Fundamentals of Molecular Biology & Gene.question: 27) Edwards syndrome is caused by:
Fundamentals of Molecular Biology & Gene.exp: Trisomy 18 is associated with clenched fists, rocker-bottom feet, severe developmental delay and high infant mortality.

Fundamentals of Molecular Biology & Gene.question: 28) Patau syndrome results from:
Fundamentals of Molecular Biology & Gene.exp: Trisomy 13 commonly presents with cleft lip/palate, microphthalmia, holoprosencephaly and polydactyly.

Fundamentals of Molecular Biology & Gene.question: 29) The inheritance pattern of cystic fibrosis is:
Fundamentals of Molecular Biology & Gene.exp: Cystic fibrosis occurs when pathogenic variants are inherited from both parents.

Fundamentals of Molecular Biology & Gene.question: 30) Hemophilia A is inherited as:
Fundamentals of Molecular Biology & Gene.exp: Hemophilia A results from factor VIII deficiency and predominantly affects males.

Fundamentals of Molecular Biology & Gene.question: 31) Sickle cell disease follows which pattern of inheritance?
Fundamentals of Molecular Biology & Gene.exp: Two abnormal β-globin genes are required for manifestation of sickle cell disease.

Fundamentals of Molecular Biology & Gene.question: 32) Marfan syndrome is inherited as:
Fundamentals of Molecular Biology & Gene.exp: Marfan syndrome is caused by mutations in the FBN1 gene and follows an autosomal dominant pattern.

Fundamentals of Molecular Biology & Gene.question: 33) Which of the following disorders is inherited as an autosomal dominant trait?
Fundamentals of Molecular Biology & Gene.exp: Achondroplasia is an autosomal dominant disorder caused by mutations in the FGFR3 gene.

Fundamentals of Molecular Biology & Gene.question: 34) Phenylketonuria is inherited as:
Fundamentals of Molecular Biology & Gene.exp: Phenylketonuria results from deficiency of phenylalanine hydroxylase and follows autosomal recessive inheritance.

Fundamentals of Molecular Biology & Gene.question: 35) A couple has one child with an autosomal recessive disorder. What is the probability that their next child will also be affected?
Fundamentals of Molecular Biology & Gene.exp: When both parents are carriers, each pregnancy has a 25% chance of producing an affected child.

Fundamentals of Molecular Biology & Gene.question: 36) Which technique is most commonly used to amplify a specific DNA sequence?
Fundamentals of Molecular Biology & Gene.exp: PCR rapidly amplifies specific DNA segments for diagnosis, research and forensic analysis.

Fundamentals of Molecular Biology & Gene.question: 37) The enzyme used in polymerase chain reaction is:
Fundamentals of Molecular Biology & Gene.exp: Taq polymerase is heat-stable and remains active during repeated heating cycles of PCR.

Fundamentals of Molecular Biology & Gene.question: 38) Reverse transcriptase is used to synthesize:
Fundamentals of Molecular Biology & Gene.exp: Reverse transcriptase produces complementary DNA (cDNA) using RNA as the template.

Fundamentals of Molecular Biology & Gene.question: 39) Which blotting technique is used to detect DNA?
Fundamentals of Molecular Biology & Gene.exp: Southern blot analysis identifies specific DNA sequences using labeled probes.

Fundamentals of Molecular Biology & Gene.question: 40) Northern blot is primarily used for detection of:
Fundamentals of Molecular Biology & Gene.exp: Northern blot detects RNA molecules and is useful for studying gene expression.

Fundamentals of Molecular Biology & Gene.question: 41) Western blot is used to detect:
Fundamentals of Molecular Biology & Gene.exp: Western blot identifies specific proteins using antibodies directed against the target protein.

Fundamentals of Molecular Biology & Gene.question: 42) Which technique is commonly used to diagnose HIV infection by detecting viral proteins?
Fundamentals of Molecular Biology & Gene.exp: Western blot has historically been used as a confirmatory test by detecting antibodies directed against HIV proteins.

Fundamentals of Molecular Biology & Gene.question: 43) A mutation that does not alter the amino acid sequence is called a:
Fundamentals of Molecular Biology & Gene.exp: Due to degeneracy of the genetic code, some nucleotide substitutions do not change the encoded amino acid.

Fundamentals of Molecular Biology & Gene.question: 44) Which laboratory technique is most appropriate for detecting numerical chromosomal abnormalities such as trisomy 21?
Fundamentals of Molecular Biology & Gene.exp: Karyotyping allows visualization of chromosome number and large structural abnormalities.

Fundamentals of Molecular Biology & Gene.question: 45) A male with tall stature, gynecomastia and infertility most likely has:
Fundamentals of Molecular Biology & Gene.exp: The classic features of Klinefelter syndrome are due to the presence of an extra X chromosome (47,XXY).

Fundamentals of Molecular Biology & Gene.question: 46) A female with short stature, webbed neck and primary amenorrhea most likely has:
Fundamentals of Molecular Biology & Gene.exp: Turner syndrome (45,X) commonly presents with short stature, gonadal dysgenesis and primary amenorrhea.

Fundamentals of Molecular Biology & Gene.question: 47) A pedigree showing affected individuals in every generation with male-to-male transmission is most consistent with:
Fundamentals of Molecular Biology & Gene.exp: Vertical transmission and father-to-son inheritance are characteristic of autosomal dominant disorders.

Fundamentals of Molecular Biology & Gene.question: 48) A pedigree in which affected males are connected through carrier females, with no father-to-son transmission, is most suggestive of:
Fundamentals of Molecular Biology & Gene.exp: X-linked recessive disorders predominantly affect males and are transmitted through carrier mothers.

Fundamentals of Molecular Biology & Gene.question: 49) A child is affected by an autosomal recessive disorder, while both parents are clinically normal. The most likely explanation is that:
Fundamentals of Molecular Biology & Gene.exp: Autosomal recessive diseases manifest when a child inherits one mutant allele from each heterozygous carrier parent.

Fundamentals of Molecular Biology & Gene.question: 50) A woman has a family history of Duchenne muscular dystrophy and seeks genetic counseling before pregnancy. The most appropriate initial molecular test is:
Fundamentals of Molecular Biology & Gene.option4: DNA analysis for mutations in the dystrophin gene
Fundamentals of Molecular Biology & Gene.exp: Molecular genetic testing identifies carrier status and supports accurate genetic counseling for X-linked disorders.
